saetze.text: Mister Hundred takes you at eighteen, and it came early, like it knew where I'd hide.
When I looked again, the yard was empty.
Just footprints in the frost, long and bare.
The one room it never looks in.
At eleven, the town walked me and Tess Lowry to the square.
On every porch, the shoes were kicked apart.
Side by side is all it leaves.
Mr. Odell rings the midnight bell, and it starts counting.
Only the sunrise bell ends Hiding Night.
"Last game of hide and seek, huh?"
She'd hide in the bell tower, higher than any window.
At home, I kicked my sneakers apart in the hall.
When I came back down, they were side by side.
If I ran, I'd end up like Owen.
If June hid me, she'd end up like Dad.
"It never looks in my room, Rabbit."
She rolled back the rug and opened the hatch.
The hatch closed over me, then the rug.
Above me, June lay down and counted, like every night.
No counting came from the square.
The boards above my face bent down.
Something finished her count, slow and deep.
